domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into looking up product or service information in knowledge bases and account screens.
length_reasoning: A simple factual question takes a couple of minutes; one needing several lookups or explanation takes about ten.
review_reasoning: A QA reviewer listens to the recorded contact, partly at higher speed, and checks the answer against the reference material.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong answer is usually corrected on a later call, but some reach the customer as wrong terms or prices and cause a complaint.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's products, policies and tools, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is reading feedback and writing a report, though the defects are also entered in the tracker.
length_reasoning: A small round with a few testers takes under an hour; a large round with many reports to dedupe and file takes most of a day.
review_reasoning: The reviewer reads the report and spot-checks a sample of filed defects against the raw feedback.
stakes_reasoning: Missed or misreported defects can reach release and cause rework, but are usually caught later and are reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product, its known defects and the team's reporting conventions, built over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into reading the policy and loss report and writing the determination in the claim system; the output is a reasoned decision in text.
length_reasoning: A clear-cut claim takes a few minutes of reading; an ambiguous loss with exclusions and endorsements takes a couple of hours.
review_reasoning: The adjuster re-reads the relevant policy clauses and the loss facts to confirm the decision.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong coverage decision means paying a claim that is not owed or denying one that is, with financial and regulatory exposure.
context_reasoning: Needs the insurer's policy forms and claims rules, learned over weeks to a few months.

domain_reasoning: Suites are written either as manual cases or as automated scripts; scripting or configuring tests in code takes most of the time for experienced testers.
length_reasoning: A small manual-case suite takes a couple of hours; an automated regression suite for a large area takes days.
review_reasoning: The QA lead reads through cases or code, checks coverage against the scope, and may run a part of it.
stakes_reasoning: Gaps in the suite let defects through to later stages, found by users or in later testing and fixed at some cost.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's behaviour, data model and test conventions, built over weeks to months.

domain_reasoning: The work is running commands and checking consoles and status pages, then logging results in a ticket system.
length_reasoning: A clean daily round takes about ten minutes; one with several faults to log takes an hour.
review_reasoning: The supervisor reads the recorded results and checks the logged tickets; the admins act on errors anyway.
stakes_reasoning: A missed error is usually found when users report it, but a missed real fault can turn into an outage.
context_reasoning: Needs the site's systems, normal readings and ticket conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into reproducing the problem, reading logs and operating the application or test tools.
length_reasoning: A familiar problem is diagnosed in a few minutes; a hard one needs a long session with log review and reproduction.
review_reasoning: A reviewer needs to listen to the session and check the conclusion against the evidence shown.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong cause sends the customer or developers down the wrong path and costs rework, but is reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product and the customer's setup, which takes weeks to build.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into using diagnostic tools, remote-control software, knowledge bases and the ticket system.
length_reasoning: A simple how-to or password reset takes a few minutes; a hardware or software fault can take half an hour.
review_reasoning: The supervisor listens to or reads the recorded contact, partly at higher speed, and checks the ticket.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong fix usually shows up as a repeat contact and is redone; some reach the user as lost work or a security slip.
context_reasoning: Needs the organisation's standard software, systems and policies, picked up in a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The worker types notes and actions into the account system while on the contact, which is operating that application.
length_reasoning: Counting the whole contact, a short inquiry runs a few minutes and a complaint with several actions runs a quarter of an hour.
review_reasoning: A QA reviewer compares the recorded contact with the logged notes.
stakes_reasoning: Poor notes cause confusion for later agents and repeat contacts, which is cheap to fix, though a missed commitment can cause a complaint.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's account system, note format and contact codes, learned in a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The output is a written ticket with steps, severity and evidence, mostly composed as text in the tracker.
length_reasoning: A clear defect takes a few minutes to write up with a screenshot; one needing narrowing down and logs takes much longer.
review_reasoning: A developer or triage lead reads the ticket and may try the reproduction steps.
stakes_reasoning: A weak report costs developers time and is clarified or reopened, though a wrongly low severity can delay a serious fix.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's components and the team's tracker conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is entering the request into the contract, address or billing system and sending the confirmation.
length_reasoning: A simple address change takes a few minutes; a contract or discontinuance with checks and exceptions takes half an hour.
review_reasoning: The reviewer compares the original request with the entered order and the confirmation.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong entry causes billing or service errors for the customer, fixed by rework; a wrong discontinuance can cut service or cause charges.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's forms, systems and rules, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is running commands and operating the machine and applications to confirm they function, then noting the ticket.
length_reasoning: A quick check of a repaired machine takes a few minutes; a new install with several functions to test takes close to an hour.
review_reasoning: The lead reads the ticket note and checks the listed tests; sometimes the user confirms directly.
stakes_reasoning: A missed fault comes back as a reopened ticket and annoyed user, which is reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs the organisation's standard builds and setups, but a skilled outsider would manage most of it.

domain_reasoning: The output is a written note of observations and recommendations, composed as text.
length_reasoning: A short note on one feature takes under half an hour; a note on a larger build with screenshots takes a few hours.
review_reasoning: A developer reads the note and checks the cited behaviour in the build.
stakes_reasoning: Poor feedback leads to unneeded changes or missed issues, which is noticed in later testing and reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's design intent and users, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is looking up requisition and invoice records and preparing the return invoice in the billing system.
length_reasoning: A straightforward return takes about ten minutes; a partial return with price or quantity mismatches takes an hour.
review_reasoning: Billing checks the return invoice against the original invoice and requisition.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong credit or charge reaches the customer and is reversed by a corrected invoice; large amounts carry financial loss.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's invoicing system, pricing and return rules, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into pulling and filtering data from the tracker and building counts and charts in other tools.
length_reasoning: A routine weekly report takes under half an hour; one with trend analysis and blockers explained takes two hours.
review_reasoning: The manager reads the report and checks a few counts against the tracker.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong count misleads project planning briefly and is corrected in the next report.
context_reasoning: Needs the project's defect workflow and status meanings, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into entering the order or cancellation in the order or billing system.
length_reasoning: A simple order or cancellation takes a few minutes; one with retention questions, options or errors takes twenty.
review_reasoning: A reviewer listens to the contact and checks the entered order or cancellation.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong order or cancellation causes billing errors and complaints that can be reversed; a wrong cancellation can lose the account.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's products, order systems and policies, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The strategy and schedule are written documents built from reading the scope and planning, with little tool operation.
length_reasoning: A small release plan takes a couple of hours; a large project with dependencies and resourcing takes days.
review_reasoning: The manager reads the plan, checks scope coverage and tests the schedule against delivery dates and resources.
stakes_reasoning: A poor plan leads to missed test coverage or a late release, which is costly but usually adjusted over time.
context_reasoning: Needs the product, team capacity, dependencies and stakeholders, built over months.
